issues.detail: Most examples and the monitoring workflow are written around Claude Code flags (--permission-mode, --allowedTools, --max-turns), with Codex and Gemini only briefly covered and no full examples for them.

scenarios.name: parallel-agents-non-overlapping-scopes
scenarios.rationale: A delivers a runnable script that launches two `claude -p` processes with `&`, captures PIDs via `$!`, writes each to its own log, waits on both, and pre-approves only the needed tools with `--permission-mode acceptEdits` and `--allowedTools` plus `--worktree`; B declines to launch and offers an in-session Agent option, and its shell option has the background/PID/log/wait pattern and acceptEdits but omits `--allowedTools`.

scenarios.name: codex-background-unit-tests
scenarios.rationale: A uses codex exec with workspace-write, & with $!, -o file, log redirect, and a follow-up to check exit code and run tests; B has most of the same but uses nohup and echoes pid, and its follow-up lacks an explicit exit-code check or independent test run (it asks Codex to run tests), plus it spends effort on not being able to run it.

scenarios.name: safe-agent-runaway-guard-and-monitor
scenarios.rationale: Response A hits nearly every rubric item: `timeout` plus `--max-turns` and `--max-budget-usd`, `--allowedTools`, a log capturing stdout and stderr, `ps -p`, `wait` with the exit code, kill by PID, and a post-run review. Response B has strong limits, logging and review but omits `wait`, checks liveness with `ps -o ... -p` rather than plain `ps -p`, kills the process group via `kill -- -PID` instead of plain `kill $AGENT_PID`, and only weakly mentions verifying the CLI (via `claude --help`).
